findings.obligation: D13 amber outlined chip; P2 amber outlined
findings.observation: AMBER is createTheme().palette.warning.main (MUI default #ed6c02). The product warning is #ff9800 (src/utils/theme/colors.ts:50; testTheme warning #ff9800). The hex assertion pins a colour the product never renders. The MuiChip-colorWarning class check is the product-independent falsifier and is sound.
findings.remediation: Derive AMBER from testTheme.palette.warning.main and render the chip under a ThemeProvider with testTheme, or from appColors.status.warning. Keep the class assertions.

findings.location: CycleTimeScatterPlotChart.outlierChip.test.tsx tests amber, names-the-lines, phone width, loading (expectAmberOutlined first)
findings.obligation: D16 accessible name and tooltip; C2 disabled chip does nothing; L4
findings.observation: expectAmberOutlined runs before the name, tooltip, count, disabled, no-click and usage assertions in four tests, so their observed failure is the colour check. The D16 RED is observed at wording layer (outlierWording.mutation, Show details. received); the disabled no-click and no-usage RED is not observed at chip layer.
findings.remediation: Put the colour check in its own it() or after the behavioural assertions; re-run the file and record each obligation's RED.

findings.obligation: D14 no popover and no extra dialog lines; boundary WorkItemsDialog props only
findings.observation: The mock destructures only title, items, open and onClose. Any extra prop or line the chart passes to the dialog is invisible, so the expected no extra lines is not falsified by any test. Not named in the falsifier list, but it is a promised expectation.
findings.remediation: Make the mock record the full props object it receives and assert its key set is exactly title, items, open, onClose. Keep the items assertion.

findings.obligation: P4 keyboard activation and focus return
findings.observation: Enter keydown calls onClick only because MUI Chip with onClick is a ButtonBase div that handles Enter on keydown. A native button would not respond to fireEvent.keyDown in jsdom, so the oracle couples to the element type. user-event 14.6.8 is installed.
findings.remediation: Use @testing-library/user-event: focus the chip, then user.keyboard Enter and user.click, which simulate native activation for both element types.

findings.location: CycleTimeScatterPlotChart.outlierList.test.tsx test lists every outlier straight from the chip
findings.observation: queryByText with the regex Open in a list or and 1 more throws Found multiple elements on the current popover, so its RED names a multiple match rather than an absent popover. Still semantic; the message is poor.
findings.remediation: Use queryAllByText with the same regex and expect length 0.

findings.location: CycleTimeScatterPlotChart.outlierViews.test.tsx test recomputes the median, the cut, the chip and the axis when the date range changes
findings.obligation: kept scenario: the cut recomputes with the date range
findings.observation: The 20-day cut and 4-day median were asserted only in the removed popover text. Membership equal to TZ-301 is now the only cut evidence, while the title still promises the cut.
findings.remediation: Pin the cut through membership at the boundary: an item one day above and one at the cut in the changed range, so the list shows the cut moved. Or drop the cut from the title.
